newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand ended a lacklustre day broadly steady, coming of the day's lows on some dollar sales from exporters during the afternoon, dealers said.
Bonds took heart from the stable currency and a further advance in U.S. Treasuries, paring early losses, despite disappointing November trade figures.
Both the forex and debt markets were extremnely quiet with many players having already deserted their desks for the beach.
"It's hardly a market at all -- just a few jobbers pushing prices around. Next week will be pretty much a waste of time," said one bond dealer.
Rand traders said the currency spent the first part of day idling, slipping lower on virtually no volume, before rallying to below 4.67 in the afternoon.
"There were some exporter dollars around but it's nothing to get excited about," said one trader with major bank.
He believed the rand could weaken next week after a strong run in the last four days.
"We might well see it weaken next week given that we've come off a long way from the 4.75 level hit last week, and it needs to bounce," he said.
The rand moved below 4.67 during the afternoon but was last trading off its best at 4.6720/6770 on the dollar from a low of 4.6805/6855 and 4.6650/6700 at 1400 GMT on Thursday.
Against the crosses, it was at 7.7777/7907 from 7.7592/7722 against sterling and at 0.3324/3330 marks from 0.3344/3349.
Bonds had started on a stronger note, building on Thursday's gains following better-than-expected November inflation figures, and helped by an advance in U.S. Treasuries.
But profit-taking gathered pace after the release of uninspiring November trade figures.
The South African Revenue Services reported a surplus of 0.38 billion rand, disappointing those who had hoped for a figure nearer one billion.
October's surplus rocketed to 3.90 billion surplus, but this was a one-off reflecting bumper exports of gold and Botswana diamonds, which are included in the common customs area data.
The benchmark R150 was last off its lows, helped by the rand and T-bonds, yielding 16.11 percent from 16.12 percent at 1400 GMT on Thursday.
On the money market, there were signs of pressure abating as the daily shortage slipped back to 10.312 billion rand from an eight-month high of 10.904 billion rand on Wednesday.
Three-month NCD rates were steady at 17.40 and 17.75 percent while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at a year high of 16.70 to 17.00 percent.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners bought a net 14.68 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Thursday after selling 128.77 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Wednesday.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 2.71 billion rand on Thursday from 3.57 billion rand on Wednesday.
-- Ben Hirschler, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
